A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same joint state–parameter flow-matching research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Darcy denoising, conditional generation, boundary-misspecification, and acoustic super-resolution experiments, including quantitative results and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on Darcy flow, elasticity, Helmholtz propagation, Stokes flow, and natural-image recoloring, with numerical comparisons, ablations, and generated samples.

M1.justification: The joint Adjoint Matching framework is retained, but v2 introduces scaled memoryless noise and replaces tail refinement with an endpoint-tilted time grid. It revises conditioning and correction architectures, adds a pixelwise correction MLP, replaces Euler guidance with guided Heun sampling, and introduces jointly evolved polynomial recoloring for latent image models.

E1.justification: v2 retains Darcy denoising and sparse-parameter guidance, adds elasticity boundary adaptation, damped-to-lossless Helmholtz adaptation, Stokes forcing mismatch, and ImageNet macaw/boathouse recoloring. The earlier transient acoustic super-resolution and reflective-boundary experiments, and Darcy boundary-misspecification scenario, are removed. Helmholtz evaluation does not retain the earlier space–time super-resolution task.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates PBFM, previously only discussed, and adds Base AM and Base AM+phi comparisons, including on retained Darcy denoising. The clean-trained FM comparator disappears from that comparison. ECI, already evaluated qualitatively on Darcy boundaries in v1, is evaluated quantitatively on elasticity; vanilla Adjoint Matching also becomes an image-generation comparator.

E3.justification: Reported Darcy discretization changes from harmonic to arithmetic permeability averaging. Backbone training changes from 500 epochs with Adam to 300 with AdamW and EMA; Darcy fine-tuning changes from 200 to 20 epochs. Evaluation replaces pointwise moment metrics with MMD and SSIM diversity, normalizes residuals against reference data, and increases Darcy residual evaluation from 128 to 256 samples.

E4.justification: v2 extends existing Darcy regularization studies into quantitative residual–diversity sweeps and adds controls testing whether joint parameter evolution helps beyond freezing or updating the inverse predictor. Appendix F.2.1 systematically varies Stokes forcing mismatch. Earlier Darcy residual-length-scale heatmaps and acoustic boundary-spike analyses are removed.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that quantitative evaluations use shared sampling seeds across methods and that random seeds were fixed where applicable. Both versions report residuals with ± quantities, without clearly defining their statistical meaning or documenting repeated training-run counts. The change establishes additional seed reporting, not additional independent runs.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the original Darcy result tables and removes acoustic and Darcy-boundary outcomes, while adding extensive results for new tasks and comparison variants. For example, its Helmholtz Table 2 reports weak residuals of 4.30 for full AM versus 8.33 for PBFM. Image experiments add qualitative recoloring findings. Revised training and residual normalization prevent interpreting updated Darcy numbers as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Lemma 1 and its proof that the scaled noise family remains memoryless for 0 ≤ kappa < 1. Appendix D.3 also introduces elasticity, complex Helmholtz, and Stokes weak-form derivations and normalization definitions. The earlier acoustic weak-form derivation is removed; the central control formulation remains.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain: weak-residual post-training, joint solution–parameter generation without paired training data, and connecting generative modeling with physics-informed learning. v2 extends the abstract and introduction to claim cross-domain utility for natural images and broadens the conclusion beyond preliminary Darcy/acoustic evidence.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the earlier emphasis on preserving permeability detail: regularization can also preserve artifacts in fragmented inverse predictions. It adds explanations of noise-scaling tradeoffs and the structural difficulty of severe Stokes forcing mismatch. Appendix E.2 explicitly acknowledges that the chosen physics mismatches disadvantage training-time PBFM, adding an important qualification to baseline interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 expands solver descriptions, architecture tables, metric implementation details, guidance/ECI pseudocode, and image reward and recoloring specifications; it also specifies Darcy noise magnitude. However, v1's inverse-predictor pretraining sample counts, training schedule, and test-function scale ranges are omitted. A new reproducibility statement promises full training-code release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: The main related-work discussion remains largely intact. v2 adds focused connections to latent flow matching, polynomial color enhancement, preference scoring, and supporting architecture, solver, and metric literature. It also explicitly positions scaled noise as an extension of Domingo-Enrich et al.; publication-year and venue updates otherwise preserve existing cited works.

P1.justification: Although much introductory and related-work prose is retained, v2 substantially rewrites the experimental narrative and architecture/numerical-method explanations. It introduces numbered method and task subsections, expands the training algorithm into detailed steps, reorganizes appendix results into configuration sweeps and sample collections, and adds reproducibility and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two columns to one and substantially redesigns the experimental presentation. It adds residual–MMD scatter plots, quantitative diversity curves, multipage configuration tables, and image sample grids; Darcy and guidance panels are replaced. The method schematic is retained and resized, while earlier acoustic and Darcy-boundary displays disappear.

improvement.justification: v1 provided limited external comparisons and little direct evidence isolating the value of joint parameter evolution. v2's Base AM controls and complete residual–MMD sweeps in Tables 10–13 substantially improve assessment of that central contribution, while Lemma 1 supports the new noise schedule. These gains outweigh losing transient-acoustic coverage and some inverse-predictor training details, although uncertainty reporting remains insufficiently specified.
